We prepare your documentation and systems, then coordinate the audit with a genuinely accredited body, so your certificate actually holds up with tender committees and buyers. Last verified 4 October 2026 — rules on this page checked against the current notifications. We update it the day a rule changes. Said plainly: ISO certification is not a government scheme and no government department issues it. It's a private, standards-based certification — and the honest value of a consultant here is preparing your systems properly and choosing a genuinely accredited certification body, not promising a shortcut. What we actually do Gap analysis — where your current practices fall short of the chosen standard Documentation — building the quality/environmental/food-safety manual, procedures and records the standard requires Staff training — so the system is actually followed, not just written down Internal audit & management review — before an external auditor ever sees it Certification-body selection — an accredited body (NABCB or another IAF-member accreditation), not an unaccredited "instant ISO" provider whose certificate tender committees increasingly reject Audit coordination — Stage 1 and Stage 2 audits, closing non-conformities, and annual surveillance support to keep the certificate valid Which standard fits Standard Covers ISO 9001 Quality management — the one most tenders and buyers ask for ISO 14001 Environmental management ISO 22000 Food safety management ISO 45001 Occupational health and safety ISO is a useful tender-eligibility and buyer-credibility tool, particularly alongside our GeM and government-tender work — but it never replaces statutory requirements like BIS, FSSAI or a Pollution NOC, which remain mandatory on their own terms regardless of ISO status. Product certification instead? BIS ISI / CRS . "IAF-accredited" changed meaning on 1 January 2026 The International Accreditation Forum (IAF) and ILAC merged into Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated , operational from 1 January 2026, which took over their multilateral arrangements. Existing IAF MLA marks remain valid through the transition. The correct 2026 description of a worthwhile certificate is: issued by a certification body accredited by a Global Accreditation Cooperation MRA signatory such as NABCB . A sales page still saying only "IAF-approved" without that chain is a warning sign. How to check an ISO certificate is genuine — 5 steps Two logos on the certificate: the certification body's and its accreditation body's (NABCB guidance: the AB logo should appear alongside the CB logo). One logo, or a "registrar" nobody can name, fails here. Accreditation body is a signatory — NABCB (India) or another member listed by the Global Accreditation Cooperation / former IAF MLA. Certification body is actually accredited by that AB for that standard — check the AB's public register (NABCB publishes its accredited CBs by scheme). The certificate number validates on IAF CertSearch (iafcertsearch.org) or the CB's own verification page, with matching scope, site and dates. Surveillance is live — a three-year certificate with no annual surveillance audit on record is lapsed even if the paper says 2027. Doubts about an Indian certificate can be referred to NABCB (nabcb@qcin.org). ISO itself does not certify anyone — a certificate "from ISO" does not exist. Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions How do I verify an ISO certificate online? Check the certificate number on IAF CertSearch (iafcertsearch.org) or the certification body's verification page; confirm the body is accredited for that standard by a Global Accreditation Cooperation (formerly IAF) signatory such as NABCB; and confirm both logos appear on the certificate. If any link in that chain is missing, the certificate will not survive a tender scrutiny. Is my IAF-accredited certificate still valid after the 2026 merger? Yes — IAF and ILAC became Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated on 1 January 2026 and existing IAF MLA marks stay valid through the transition. What changes is the name to look for on accreditation registers. Does ISO itself issue certificates? No. ISO publishes the standards; independent certification bodies audit and certify, and accreditation bodies (NABCB in India) accredit those certifiers. 'ISO-issued' certificates are a red flag. Is ISO certification a government registration? No. ISO standards are published by the International Organization for Standardization, and certificates are issued by private certification bodies — ideally ones accredited by NABCB (India) or another IAF-member accreditation body. No ministry or government department issues an ISO certificate. How do I check if an ISO certificate is genuine? Confirm that the certification body itself is accredited — by NABCB or another IAF-member accreditation body — and verify the certificate against that accreditation body's public database. A growing number of 'instant ISO' certificates from non-accredited bodies are now being rejected by tender committees. Which ISO standard do I actually need? ISO 9001 (quality management) is the one most tenders and buyers ask for. ISO 14001 covers environmental management, ISO 22000 covers food safety, and ISO 45001 covers occupational health and safety — the right one depends on your industry and what your buyers or tenders specifically require. Is ISO a substitute for BIS, FSSAI or Pollution NOC? No — these are separate statutory requirements under Indian law and remain mandatory regardless of ISO status. ISO is a voluntary management-system certification that complements, but never replaces, your legal compliance obligations. What does the certification process actually involve? A gap analysis against the chosen standard, building or updating your documented procedures and records, staff training, an internal audit and management review, then a Stage 1 and Stage 2 audit by your chosen accredited certification body, closing any non-conformities they raise, and ongoing annual surveillance audits to keep the certificate active. © 2026 Udyog Growth. We handle EPF registration (20+ employees), ESIC registration (10+ employees, ₹21,000 wage ceiling), and factory/contract-labour licensing under the new OSH Code thresholds — correctly, not under the old superseded rules. Last verified 4 October 2026 — rules on this page checked against the current notifications. We update it the day a rule changes. The change most businesses haven't registered: India's labour law is no longer the Factories Act, the EPF Act, the ESI Act and the Contract Labour Act as separate statutes. All of it was consolidated into four Labour Codes — the Code on Wages, the Industrial Relations Code, the Code on Social Security, and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH) Code — which came into force together on 21 November 2025. Final Central Rules were notified on 8-9 May 2026. State rules are still being finalised in several states, including (by some accounts) Delhi, UP, Haryana and Bihar — we verify your state's current status before filing. What actually changed, and what didn't Area Old threshold/rule Current (OSH Code / Codes) Factory licence (with power) 10+ workers 20+ workers Factory licence (without power) 20+ workers 40+ workers Contract labour licence Contractor needs licence at 20+ workers 50+ workers; principal employer's single OSH registration covers contract labour engagement EPF coverage 20+ employees, ₹15,000 wage ceiling Unchanged — 20+ employees, ₹15,000 ceiling ESIC coverage 10+ employees (notified areas), ₹21,000 ceiling ₹21,000 ceiling unchanged; "notified area" restriction removed on paper under the Social Security Code Wage definition Basic + DA could be structured low Basic + DA must be at least 50% of total remuneration — raises the PF/ESI/gratuity base Licence validity Typically 1-5 years, state-dependent Up to 5 years under the OSH Code, with deemed approval if authorities miss prescribed timelines The ₹21,000 ESIC ceiling and ₹15,000 EPF ceiling have not changed despite widely-shared claims online — we confirm current figures against the actual notification before advising a client, not against what's trending. Shop Act, EPF & ESIC by city The EPF and ESIC thresholds are national; the Shop Act threshold is not. City pages with the current rule and the right portal: Noida & Greater Noida (UP — 20+) · Gurugram & Faridabad (Haryana — 20+, s.13A below) · Patna (Bihar — no threshold, Professional Tax levied). EPFO establishment registration Online registration via the EPFO Unified Portal using PAN/incorporation details and a digital signature. Once registered, ongoing employer obligations include generating and linking a UAN for every new joinee, seeding and verifying Aadhaar/bank KYC, filing the monthly Electronic Challan-cum-Return (ECR) by the 15th, and processing exit dates correctly. The new 50% basic-and-DA wage rule is the most common query we're handling in 2026 — it changes the contribution base even where headcount and salary haven't changed. ESIC establishment registration Online registration on the ESIC portal; every covered employee must be registered within 10 days of joining, with monthly contributions (0.75% employee + 3.25% employer) due by the 15th. We handle registration, monthly filing, and the compliance review that catches whether your current wage structuring actually keeps you under or over the ₹21,000 threshold correctly. Factory and establishment registration under the OSH Code Units crossing the 20/40-worker threshold need factory registration; units with 10+ workers below that threshold still need OSH Code establishment registration. The Code allows a single combined licence covering factory, contract labour and beedi-establishment matters, valid up to 5 years, with a 30-day deemed-approval clock on plan/expansion permission. State delivery channels vary — Delhi's Labour Department portal, UP's Nivesh Mitra 3.0, Haryana's HEPC/Invest Haryana window, and Bihar's Single Window Clearance System are the relevant routes, though plan approval and stability certificates remain physical-engineering steps everywhere. Delhi Shop Act status (checked 4 October 2026): the Delhi Shops & Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2026 — which raises the registration threshold to 20 employees, matching UP and Haryana — was published on 11 March 2026 but its commencement date has not been notified . Until that notification appears in the Gazette, a Delhi establishment of any size still registers with the Labour Department, GNCTD. Vendors applying the UP/Haryana rule to Delhi are wrong today. Check your own position in 10 seconds with the Shop Act applicability checker ; we update this box the day the commencement is notified. Delhi-specific page: Delhi Shop Act registration — what applies today and when the 20-employee rule starts . Shop & Establishment Act registration This remains a state-law registration — it was not replaced by the central Labour Codes. Delhi, UP, Haryana (under the Punjab Shops & Commercial Establishments Act as applicable) and Bihar each have their own Act and registration process. We file this correctly under your specific state's current rules rather than assuming a one-size answer across NCR. Is your salary structure compliant with the 50% rule? Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions Are the Factories Act and Contract Labour Act still in force? No — both are subsumed in the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH) Code, 2020, which took effect on 21 November 2025 along with the other three Labour Codes. Final Central Rules were notified on 8-9 May 2026. State rules determine the actual forms and procedures and are still being finalised in several states — we check your state's current status before filing anything. At how many employees do I need EPF and ESIC? EPF applies at 20 or more employees, with mandatory coverage for employees earning up to ₹15,000/month. ESIC applies at 10 or more employees (20 in some states) for employees earning up to ₹21,000/month gross (₹25,000 for persons with disability). Has the ESIC wage ceiling increased to ₹30,000? No. The ₹21,000 ceiling remains in force under the existing notification. A ₹30,000 ceiling has been discussed as a proposal but has not been notified — any site or advisor telling you otherwise is quoting an unconfirmed figure. Do I need a factory licence for 15 workers using power? Not under the current OSH Code thresholds, which set factory licensing at 20+ workers with power (40+ without). You still need OSH Code establishment registration at 10+ workers and must follow applicable safety provisions regardless. Does my contractor need a separate labour licence? Only if they deploy 50 or more contract workers — the threshold was raised from 20. Your own single OSH Code establishment registration already covers your engagement of contract labour; you no longer need a separate CLRA registration as principal employer. What changed in how salary is structured for PF/ESI purposes? Under the Code on Wages, basic pay plus dearness allowance must now be at least 50% of total remuneration. This raises the base on which PF, ESI and gratuity are calculated for many employers who had structured salaries with a large non-basic component — it's the single most common compliance gap we're finding in 2026. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Compliance-first documentation — built to withstand scrutiny, protecting your business from future audits or objections. Frequently Asked Questions How much is the CLU fee in Haryana in 2026? Scrutiny fee is ₹10 per sq m of site (₹2 per sq m for industrial or recreational use); the real cost is the conversion charges, EDC and IDC raised at the Letter of Intent stage, set by the TCP schedule for the zone and use. A petrol pump already operating without CLU pays a ₹2,00,000 composition fee on regularisation. Do I still need Section 80 conversion in Noida or Ghaziabad after the 2026 amendment? Inside development-authority, industrial-authority, regulated and Awas Vikas areas — no: a sanctioned building plan is deemed conversion under the March 2026 reform. Outside those areas the SDM route under Section 80 (2% of circle rate, 45-day standard) still applies. Does the Bihar land conversion Act apply inside Patna Municipal Corporation? No — the 2010 Act excludes municipal areas constituted under the Bihar Municipal Act, 2007. Inside Patna's municipal limits, land use follows the master plan and building-plan sanction through the development authority; outside them, the SDO conversion at 10% of market value applies. Is MPD-2041 or MPD-2047 the current Delhi master plan? MPD-2047 — notified on 20 August 2026 as an extensive modification of MPD-2021. MPD-2041 was drafted but never notified; guides and FAQs still describing it as 'awaiting notification' are out of date. Who grants change of land use (CLU) in Gurugram or Faridabad? DTCP Haryana — the application goes on Form CLU-I to the Director, Town & Country Planning, and is scrutinised against the development plan for your zone. Typical processing is 60–90 days, faster in pre-cleared industrial zones. We verify zone permissibility before you buy, not after. How is agricultural land converted in Bihar, and what does it cost? Fully online at landconversion.bihar.gov.in under the Bihar Agriculture Land (Conversion) Act 2010 — the SDM is the competent authority, the fee is 10% of the circle-rate value, and the service standard is 90 days. You need an updated Jamabandi, current Lagaan Rasid and a self-declaration of all landholders stating the purpose. Can I build a factory or warehouse on agricultural land without conversion? No — construction or non-agricultural use without conversion/CLU risks penalties, demolition proceedings and an unfinanceable, unsellable title. Banks also won't lend against unconverted land for a commercial project. Conversion is the first approval in the sequence, before pollution consents and building plans. Is any land use exempt from conversion in Bihar? Yes — notable exemptions include household micro-industry on up to 1 acre and small shops up to 500 sq ft, among others under the Act. Whether your exact use qualifies depends on the plot's record and purpose; we check this first, because an exemption saves both the 10% fee and the wait. What documents drive a CLU / conversion application? Ownership record (Jamabandi/mutation), latest rent receipt or land-revenue proof, plot map, the intended-use declaration, and — for Haryana CLU — the site plan against the zone's development plan. Mismatched ownership records are the most common reason files stall; we fix the record before filing. My land is in Bihar but I live in Delhi-NCR — can you handle it end to end? Yes. Bihar's process is online, and our practice spans both Delhi-NCR and Bihar — we prepare the record, file on the portal, pay the fee, respond to SDM-level queries and follow the matter to the conversion order without you travelling. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Compliance-first documentation — built to withstand scrutiny, protecting your business from future audits or objections. Frequently Asked Questions Is a new Delhi excise policy in force for 2026-27? No. With the new policy not finalised, the Excise Department ordered renewal and grant of hotel, club and restaurant licences for 2026-27 on the same terms as 2025-26, with a 10% fee increase for the L-17/L-18/L-19/L-20 families and the right to review fees further. We track the policy file and update this page the day a new policy is notified. Can I open a private liquor shop (retail vend) in Delhi? No — under the current excise regime (extended to 31 March 2027), retail liquor sale in Delhi is restricted to four government corporations (DTTDC, DSIIDC, DSCSC, DCCWS). Private individuals cannot get a retail vend licence right now. Private opportunity is in restaurant/bar (L-17), hotel (L-15/L-16), club (L-28), wholesale (L-1), and event permits (P-10/P-13). Which license does my restaurant need to serve alcohol in Delhi? An independent restaurant needs an L-17 licence (with the L-17F add-on for foreign liquor). Your premises must be in a commercial area, Tourism-approved, and meet Rule 51 distance norms (100m from schools, religious places and hospitals), with fire and municipal approvals in place. Hotels use L-15/L-16 instead; clubs use L-28. How much does a restaurant liquor license cost in Delhi? L-17 fees are annual and scale with your seating and category; HCR-category fees (L-17/L-18/L-19/L-20) were raised 10% for 2026-27. We give you a current, category-specific estimate after reviewing your premises rather than quoting a generic number that may already be outdated. How do I get a liquor permit for a wedding or party in Delhi? Apply for a P-10 permit — Rs 5,000 for most venues, Rs 15,000 for banquet halls, motels and farmhouses. Liquor must be purchased from an authorised Delhi vend (keep the original bill), served only to guests above 25, and kept screened from public view. We handle the e-Abkari filing so it's approved before your date. Where are Delhi liquor license applications filed? Online, through the e-Abkari portal (eabkari.delhi.gov.in) — physical-only submissions were discontinued in 2017. The flow is: create an EXD ID, select the license form, upload documents and layout plans, pay fees, then clear a premises inspection before the license is granted. My liquor license application was rejected — what can I do? Rejections commonly cite eligibility issues, pending investigations, distance-rule violations, or incomplete documents. Delhi's courts have repeatedly directed applicants to first appeal to the Appellate/Financial Commissioner under the Excise Act rather than going straight to court. We diagnose the actual ground for rejection and file a reasoned appeal. Is Delhi's new liquor policy in force yet? Not as of August 2026. A new policy (modern/premium stores) is still in draft under a government committee. The current duty-based regime — in place since September 2022 — has been extended repeatedly and now runs to 31 March 2027. We track this and update clients the moment anything actually changes, rather than reacting to rumours. What is the legal drinking age and personal possession limit in Delhi? The legal drinking age in Delhi is 25 (Section 23, Delhi Excise Act, 2009). Without a permit, you may possess up to 9 litres of Indian/foreign spirits or 18 litres of wine/beer; to hold more, you need an L-30 personal permit. Do I need a permit to serve alcohol at a house party in Delhi? At your own residence — no permit is needed to serve guests and family, as long as the liquor stays within your personal possession limit. The moment the event moves outside your residence — a farmhouse, banquet hall or any other premises — a P-10 permit is required even if the quantity is within the possession limit. That distinction catches many hosts off guard. What is the P-13 permit, and how is it different from P-10? P-13 is for premises that already hold a liquor licence — hotels, restaurants and clubs hosting a one-day function, at a Rs 5,000 permit fee. P-10 is for everyone else: serving liquor at a party, wedding or event on unlicensed premises, at Rs 5,000 for general venues and Rs 15,000 for motels, banquet halls and farmhouses. Note the service age at such events is 25 years, not 21. What is the L-30 licence, and who actually needs it? L-30 is Delhi's home-stock licence: if you want to keep liquor at your residence above the individual free possession limit (9 litres of spirits / 18 litres of wine and beer), you apply for an L-30 grant and renew it periodically with the Excise Department. It's relevant for collectors and serious home bars — without it, excess stock at home is an excise violation. Who is eligible for the L-28 club licence? Only a club formally registered with the Registrar of Firms or Registrar of Cooperative Societies — and the licence permits service of liquor strictly to the club's own members within club premises, with stock procured from authorised sources. What it unlocks is not small: subsidised credit, collateral-free guarantees, procurement preferences and certification support. Most businesses register and stop. We register — and then extract every benefit the status carries. Where the money actually is Scheme What it gives you Udyam Registration New registration, amendments, correct classification (micro/small/medium decides your benefits), certification guidance PMEGP 15–35% margin-money subsidy on project cost for new units CGTMSE Collateral-free loans; guarantee ceiling doubled to ₹10 crore (w.e.f. 1 April 2025), annual fees cut sharply ZED Certification Quality & environmental certification, subsidised cost — valuable for buyers and government procurement. For broader quality credentials, see our ISO certification and BIS certification services Lean Manufacturing Competitiveness Scheme Productivity and cost-reduction programs for manufacturing units MSE-CDP Cluster development — common facility centres and infrastructure, with government coordination International Cooperation Scheme Export promotion, trade fair participation, delegation support The stack effect: these schemes compound. A food unit with Udyam + CGTMSE + PMFME support and a GeM listing operates with subsidised capital, no collateral pressure and a direct line to government buyers. We build the whole stack, not one certificate. Udyam registration — the actual process, start to end Before you pay anyone ₹199 for a "24-hour MSME certificate": Udyam registration on udyamregistration.gov.in is free , Aadhaar-OTP based, and the certificate is generated the same day. Dozens of look-alike portals charge for it and some issue a "certificate" that is not a Udyam number at all. What you pay a consultant for is classification under the 1 April 2025 limits (micro ≤ ₹2.5 cr / ₹10 cr; small ≤ ₹25 cr / ₹100 cr; medium ≤ ₹125 cr / ₹500 cr), the NIC-code choices that decide scheme eligibility, and everything after the certificate — CGTMSE, Samadhaan, ZED, tenders. Quick check: MSME classifier . Check what you need. Just an Aadhaar number of the proprietor/managing partner/karta, and PAN + GSTIN of the enterprise (linked automatically for investment and turnover figures via IT and GST records — no documents to upload). Apply on udyamregistration.gov.in. Aadhaar OTP verification, then enterprise details — name, type, address, bank account, main activity (manufacturing/service), and NIC codes for what you actually do. Classification is automatic. Investment and turnover pulled from linked PAN/GST records decide Micro, Small or Medium — you don't self-declare figures. Udyam Registration Number issued immediately on submission, with the e-certificate available for download right after — no waiting period, no renewal ever required. Then the real work starts. A URN alone doesn't claim anything — CGTMSE, PMEGP, ZED, and the Section 43B(h) payment-timeline protection all need to be actively invoked with the right paperwork. This is where most businesses stop short and where we pick up. Udyam limits (revised 1 Apr 2025): Micro — investment ₹2.5 crore / turnover ₹10 crore; Small — ₹25 crore / ₹100 crore; Medium — ₹125 crore / ₹500 crore. The higher of the two criteria governs classification. Section 43B(h) leverage: buyers must pay Micro & Small suppliers within 45 days or lose the tax deduction — your Udyam certificate is now a receivables weapon, not just a registration. PMEGP: 15% (general-urban) to 35% (special-rural) margin-money subsidy; project caps ₹50 lakh manufacturing / ₹20 lakh services; 10% own contribution; Udyam is required before physical verification. CGTMSE: guarantee cover 75–85%; annual guarantee fee from 0.37% p.a. (rising to ~1.20% for ₹8–10 crore loans). ZED: three levels (Bronze/Silver/Gold), 3-year validity, plus a ₹10,000 joining reward on taking the ZED pledge. CLCSS (technology upgrade): 15% upfront capital subsidy on machinery loans up to ₹1 crore (cap ₹15 lakh), credited straight into your loan account, across 51 approved sub-sectors — food processing, auto components, pharma, packaging, printing and more. CGTMSE (2026 update): retail and wholesale trading enterprises are now CGTMSE-eligible too; loans up to ₹2 crore need zero collateral security. Mudra loans: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (up to ₹5 lakh), Tarun (up to ₹10 lakh), and Tarun Plus (up to ₹20 lakh, for those who've repaid a Tarun loan) — no collateral, for any non-farm income-generating activity. The NCR nuance most consultants skip: Delhi-NCR is one market but three states. Udyam, PMEGP, CGTMSE and ZED are central — identical whether you sit in Delhi, Noida/Ghaziabad (UP) or Gurugram/Faridabad (Haryana). But state-level industrial incentives differ on each side of the border, so where your unit physically sits inside NCR can change what you're entitled to. We map both layers — central and state — before you claim anything. Food-sector MSMEs: your FSSAI registration or license sits alongside Udyam in nearly every scheme file — we set up both together. Getting your money out — delayed payments & invoice discounting Two levers most MSMEs never use. First, MSME Samadhaan : under the MSMED Act, a buyer must pay a registered micro or small enterprise within a maximum of 45 days — no contract can extend it further — and beyond that owes compound interest at three times the RBI bank rate , with monthly rests. A complaint filed on the Samadhaan portal goes to your state's MSE Facilitation Council (MSEFC), which is required to decide within 90 days, and a buyer cannot challenge the award in court without first depositing 75% of the awarded amount. Buyers also lose the income-tax deduction on payments held beyond the limit — real pressure that gets invoices cleared. Second, TReDS : the RBI-regulated invoice-discounting platforms (RXIL, M1xchange, Invoicemart) where you sell verified receivables to financiers and get paid now — no collateral, without recourse to you. Since the MSME Ministry's November 2024 notification, every company above ₹250 crore turnover and every CPSE is mandated onto TReDS, which means your large buyers are already on the platform. We handle Samadhaan filings, MSEFC representation and TReDS onboarding end to end. Illustrative client engagement — details anonymised. Compliance-first documentation — built to withstand scrutiny, protecting your business from future audits or objections. Frequently Asked Questions Is Udyam registration free? Yes, Udyam registration on the government portal is free of government fees. Our service covers correct classification, documentation, amendments and using the registration to actually unlock scheme benefits — where most businesses stop short. How much subsidy does PMEGP give? PMEGP provides margin money subsidy of 15–35% of project cost depending on category (general/special) and location (urban/rural) for new manufacturing and service units, routed through banks with KVIC/KVIB/DIC as implementing agencies. What is CGTMSE and how does it help? CGTMSE provides a credit guarantee to banks for collateral-free loans to micro and small enterprises — now up to ₹10 crore (ceiling doubled w.e.f. 1 April 2025) — meaning you can access working capital and term loans without pledging property. We prepare the proposal and coordinate the bank process. What is ZED certification? Zero Defect Zero Effect certification under the MSME Ministry recognises quality and environmental standards, improves buyer credibility (including in government procurement) and comes with subsidised certification costs for MSMEs. What is CLCSS and how much subsidy does it give? CLCSS (Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme) gives Micro and Small enterprises a 15% upfront capital subsidy when they take a loan to upgrade plant and machinery, capped at Rs 15 lakh on institutional finance up to Rs 1 crore. The subsidy is credited directly into your loan account through the financing bank, reducing your outstanding principal from day one. Which Mudra loan category should I apply for? Shishu suits very early-stage needs up to Rs 50,000; Kishor fits an established but growing business up to Rs 5 lakh; Tarun covers expansion up to Rs 10 lakh; and Tarun Plus, up to Rs 20 lakh, is for businesses that have already repaid a Tarun loan responsibly. All are collateral-free for eligible non-farm income-generating activities. What happens if my turnover crosses the MSME limit after I register? Udyam re-classifies automatically based on your filed turnover and investment data; you don't lose past benefits, but future eligibility follows the new classification. We help you plan scheme applications before a threshold crossing changes what you qualify for. Can a service business (not manufacturing) register under Udyam and claim these schemes? Yes — Udyam, CGTMSE, PMEGP (with sector-specific caps) and ZED all cover eligible service enterprises, not just manufacturing; the investment/turnover test is what matters, not the sector label. How long does Udyam registration take? It's instant — the Udyam Registration Number and e-certificate are generated immediately on submission, since classification is pulled automatically from your linked PAN and GST records. There's no waiting period and no renewal requirement. Can I register more than one business with the same Aadhaar? No — one Aadhaar number can hold only one Udyam Registration. If you run multiple units or branches under the same PAN, add them as additional activities/units within that single registration rather than creating a second one. Is Udyog Aadhaar the same as Udyam registration? No — Udyog Aadhaar was the older system, discontinued and replaced by Udyam Registration. If you still hold an Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM), it needs to be migrated to Udyam to keep accessing MSME benefits; the two aren't interchangeable going forward. How do I download my Udyam certificate if I've lost it? Go to udyamregistration.gov.in, select Print/Verify Certificate, enter your Udyam Registration Number and registered mobile/email for OTP verification, and download the PDF. If you've also lost the URN itself, recovery runs through the same portal using your linked Aadhaar or PAN — we handle this recovery for clients when the original registration details have gone missing. My business operates across Delhi-NCR — do I need separate Udyam registrations for Delhi, Noida and Gurugram? No. Udyam is PAN-linked: one registration covers the whole enterprise nationally, and your Delhi, UP and Haryana premises are added as units within that single registration. What changes across the NCR borders is state-level incentives, not your Udyam status — we structure the registration so every location is correctly reflected. A buyer hasn't paid my MSME invoice for months — what can I actually do? File a delayed-payment complaint on the MSME Samadhaan portal — it goes to your state's MSE Facilitation Council (MSEFC), which must decide within 90 days. You need a valid Udyam registration and your invoices/proof of supply. The claim isn't just the principal: the buyer owes compound interest at three times the RBI bank rate from the due date, and can't challenge the award without depositing 75% of it first. We prepare the file and represent you before the Council. What interest can I claim on a delayed MSME payment? Compound interest at three times the bank rate notified by RBI, with monthly rests, running from the day payment fell due — and the credit period can never lawfully exceed 45 days from acceptance, regardless of what the contract says. On a large pending invoice this interest becomes substantial, which is exactly why a well-drafted Samadhaan claim gets buyers to settle. What is TReDS, and should my MSME register on it? TReDS platforms (RXIL, M1xchange, Invoicemart) let you sell your verified, buyer-accepted invoices to banks and financiers and receive payment immediately — no collateral, and without recourse, meaning if the buyer later defaults it's the financier's problem, not yours. Since companies above ₹250 crore turnover and all CPSEs are now mandated onto TReDS, your biggest buyers are likely already there. We handle the seller-side onboarding and first discounting cycle. How much PMEGP subsidy will I get, and is there a second loan? Margin-money subsidy runs 15%–35%: general category gets 15% (urban) / 25% (rural), and special categories (SC/ST/OBC/minorities/women/ex-servicemen/PH/NER) get 25% (urban) / 35% (rural), on projects up to Rs 50 lakh (manufacturing) or Rs 20 lakh (services). Successful units can also take a second PMEGP loan for upgradation — up to Rs 1 crore (manufacturing) / Rs 25 lakh (services) at 15% subsidy — after about three years of clean operation. What does ZED certification actually cost after subsidy? Certification fees are Bronze Rs 10,000, Silver Rs 40,000, Gold Rs 90,000 — but a Micro enterprise gets 80% subsidy (Small 60%, Medium 50%), plus 10% extra for women/SC/ST-owned or NER/aspirational-district units and 5% more for SFURTI/MSE-CDP cluster units. With the Rs 10,000 joining reward, Bronze is effectively free. Some banks also give interest concessions to ZED-certified borrowers, so the certificate can pay for itself. Is ECLGS still available in 2026? Yes — but it's a new avatar. ECLGS 5.0, approved by the Cabinet in May 2026, is a fresh Rs 18,100-crore guarantee window (targeting Rs 2.55 lakh crore of credit) for businesses hit by the West Asia crisis — not the old COVID scheme. Eligible standard accounts (as of 31 March 2026) can get additional credit up to 20% of Q4 FY26 peak working capital, capped at Rs 100 crore, with 100% guarantee for MSMEs, 5-year tenor with a 1-year moratorium, nil guarantee fee, running to 31 March 2027. © 2026 Udyog Growth. The registration sequence — and what each one unlocks Step Typical timeline Choose structure (Trust / Society / Section 8) Decided upfront, not by filing speed NGO Darpan (NITI Aayog) ~7–10 working days, free 12A registration Filed via Form 10A 80G registration Usually processed alongside 12A CSR-1 (MCA) Unlocks corporate CSR funding FCRA (only if needed) 90–120 working days; requires 3 years' track record Choose the structure. Trust, Society, or Section 8 Company — decided by how you'll operate and fund, not by which is fastest to file. NGO Darpan (NITI Aayog). Free, ~7-10 working days — generates the ID that later registrations and many donors will ask for. 12A registration. Exempts your NGO's income from tax when used for charitable purposes — filed via Form 10A on the Income Tax portal. 80G registration. Lets your donors claim a tax deduction on their contribution — usually processed alongside 12A, and often the deciding factor for a hesitant corporate or individual donor. CSR-1 (MCA). Unlocks corporate CSR funding specifically — without this filing, a company legally cannot route CSR money to you, no matter how willing they are. FCRA, only if needed. For foreign contributions — requires 3 years' existence and ₹15 lakh in documented core-activity spend, a dedicated FCRA account specifically at SBI's Sansad Marg branch in New Delhi, and runs 90-120 working days with a ₹10,000 government fee. Every key functionary (Chairperson, Secretary, Treasurer, all trustees/directors) must provide Aadhaar and clear a background check — missing even one is an automatic rejection ground. Once granted, FCRA is valid 5 years; renewal (Form FC-3C) must be filed at least 6 months before expiry, or you must stop receiving and spending foreign funds until it's renewed. We flag this early if foreign funding is part of your plan, since the eligibility clock only starts once you meet the track record. The sequencing mistake we see most: NGOs that chase FCRA or big CSR partners before 12A/80G are in place — donors and companies ask for these certificates before committing, so getting the tax-registration stack right first is what actually opens funding conversations, not a detail to handle later. 2026 update — "FCRA 2.0" — if you already hold FCRA registration, read this now: The FCRA Amendment Rules 2026, in force from 22 June 2026, require every existing FCRA-registered NGO to file a new Form FC-6F specifying the exact purposes and states/UTs your registration covers — within one year (by around 21 June 2027) — or risk cancellation. This isn't optional paperwork: it's a compliance deadline with real teeth. Renewal now also carries a ₹10 lakh utilisation benchmark and expanded disclosure requirements. If your FCRA registration predates this change, we assess your current approval scope, prepare the FC-6F filing, and file it well before the window closes — waiting until month 11 is how NGOs lose registration over a filing, not a violation. Registering in Delhi, Noida or Gurugram — what changes and what doesn't: society and trust registration is state-level, so the registrar differs depending on which side of the NCR border you incorporate. But everything that funders actually check — 12A, 80G, NGO Darpan, CSR-1 and FCRA — is central and identical across NCR. Being in the capital region also puts you closest to where national CSR head offices and the FCRA process itself are based. We advise on the registration state first, then run the central approvals in the right sequence. Forming a Trust, Society or Section 8 company to run a school? Delhi-NCR entities fall under the Commissioner of Income Tax (Exemptions), Delhi; Patna entities under CIT (Exemptions), Patna. There is no government fee for Form 10A or 10AB. 50% or 100%? Most 80G-approved NGOs give donors a 50% deduction, subject to the qualifying-limit rules; 100% deduction applies only to specified funds and institutions named in the Act. Telling donors "100%" when your approval is in the 50% category is the most common 80G misstatement we see on NGO websites — and it comes up at renewal. 12A / 80G under the Income-tax Act, 2025 — the new numbers Old (1961 Act) New (2025 Act, from 1 April 2026) What it is Section 12A / 12AB Section 332 Registration of the trust/institution for exemption Section 80G Section 354 Donor deduction approval Form 10A Form 104 Provisional application Form 10AB Form 105 Regular / renewal application — Forms 106 / 107 Provisional order / final order Form 10BE Form 114 Donor certificate Form 10B / 10BB Form 112 Audit report Validity is unchanged in substance — provisional 3 years, regular 5 years — with a 10-year term for smaller trusts (income up to ₹5 crore) on the registration side; 80G approval stays at 5 years. Pages still telling you to file "Form 10A" are quoting the repealed Act. FCRA after the 2026 Rules — what changed on 22 June 2026 Registration is now specific to purpose and State/UT — foreign contribution can be used only for the purposes and in the states covered by your certificate Existing registrants must file Form FC-6F by 21 June 2027 to align their registration with the new regime Renewal needs evidence of use: at least ₹10 lakh of foreign contribution utilised over the previous two financial years (new Rule 14A) Prior-permission tranches: 75% utilisation of the earlier tranche plus a field inquiry before the next is released Additional disclosure obligations, including on publications Separately, the FCRA (Amendment) Bill, 2026 — vesting of assets on cessation, revised penalties — was introduced on 25 March 2026 and is still pending ; treat it as proposed law, not current law. Frequently Asked Questions Which form do I file for provisional 12A/80G now — Form 10A or Form 104? Form 104 (provisional) and Form 105 (regular/renewal) under the Income-tax Act, 2025, in force from 1 April 2026; 12A is now Section 332 and 80G is Section 354. Existing approvals carry over; new applications use the new forms. What is the minimum foreign contribution utilisation needed for FCRA renewal under the 2026 Rules? At least ₹10 lakh of foreign contribution utilised over the previous two financial years (Rule 14A, FCRA Amendment Rules 2026). Associations below that are unlikely to be renewed — plan utilisation and reporting two years ahead of expiry. Do existing FCRA-registered NGOs need to file anything new by June 2027? Yes — Form FC-6F by 21 June 2027, declaring the purposes and States/UTs the registration will cover under the new purpose- and state-specific regime. My provisional 80G expires in 2026 — when must I apply for regular registration? File Form 10AB at least six months before the provisional certificate expires, or within six months of starting activities, whichever is earlier. Missing that window means a fresh provisional application and a gap donors notice. Do my donors get a 50% or 100% deduction? For most 80G-approved NGOs, 50% subject to the qualifying limit. 100% applies only to specified funds and institutions named in the Act. Check your approval order before telling donors otherwise. Which office handles 12A/80G for a Delhi or Noida NGO? The Commissioner of Income Tax (Exemptions), Delhi, for NCR entities; CIT (Exemptions), Patna for Bihar. Filing is online on the e-filing portal; queries and hearings come from that office. Should I register as a Trust, Society, or Section 8 Company? It depends on how you'll operate: a Trust suits a small, founder-led charitable purpose; a Society fits a membership-based organisation with a managing committee; a Section 8 Company suits larger NGOs wanting a corporate structure, easier bank/donor trust, and cleaner CSR eligibility. We assess your actual activities and funding plans before recommending one, since converting later is far more work than choosing correctly at the start. What's the difference between 12A and 80G registration? 12A exempts your NGO's own income from income tax, provided it's used for charitable purposes. 80G is what benefits your donors — it lets them claim a tax deduction (typically 50%) on what they give you, which is often the single biggest driver of individual and corporate donations. Both are filed via Form 10A on the Income Tax e-filing portal and are generally valid for 5 years, needing renewal before expiry. Do I need FCRA registration? Only if you intend to receive foreign contributions — domestic donations, government grants, and CSR funding don't require it. FCRA registration (Ministry of Home Affairs) needs your NGO to have existed for at least 3 years with a minimum of Rs 15 lakh spent on core charitable activities, plus a dedicated FCRA bank account (mandatorily with SBI's designated branch) kept separate from your regular account. Approval typically takes 90-120 working days, so this isn't something to start once foreign funding is already on the table. What is CSR-1 and why does it matter for funding? Form CSR-1, filed with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, is mandatory before an NGO can receive CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) funds from companies — it generates a unique CSR Registration Number that corporate donors will ask for. Without it, even a willing corporate funder legally cannot route CSR money to you. What is NGO Darpan and is it mandatory? NGO Darpan is a free registration on NITI Aayog's portal that generates a unique ID — it's required for accessing central government grant schemes and is increasingly asked for by CSR donors and crowdfunding platforms too, even when not strictly mandatory for that specific channel. It's typically the first registration we complete, since several later steps reference the Darpan ID. What documents do I need ready before 12A/80G registration? Your registration certificate (trust deed, society bylaws, or Section 8 incorporation), PAN, financial statements if you've been operating more than a year, notes on your activities and objectives, and NGO Darpan details if already registered. Missing or inconsistent documents are the most common cause of processing delays here. Does NGO Darpan registration also cover FCRA compliance? No — they're separate. NGO Darpan (NITI Aayog) is a prerequisite for FCRA and is required in the FCRA application form, but registering there doesn't grant any FCRA approval. You still need to apply for FCRA separately once you meet its 3-year/₹15 lakh eligibility. What happens if my FCRA registration lapses? You must stop receiving and spending foreign funds immediately until it's renewed — Form FC-3C, filed at least 6 months before your 5-year registration expires, is what keeps it current. A late renewal application risks a compliance gap that can affect ongoing foreign-funded projects. What is Form FC-6F and do I need to file it? Form FC-6F is a new filing required under the FCRA Amendment Rules 2026 (in force from 22 June 2026) for every NGO that already holds FCRA registration — not new applicants. It specifies the exact purposes and states/UTs your foreign-contribution activity covers. You have one year from the rules taking effect (until approximately 21 June 2027) to file it; missing the deadline risks cancellation of your existing registration. My FCRA registration is old — does FCRA 2.0 change anything for renewal? Yes. Beyond the FC-6F filing, renewal now carries a ₹10 lakh utilisation benchmark and expanded disclosure requirements. If your registration is approaching its 5-year renewal alongside this new filing requirement, we handle both together so you're not caught filing twice in close succession. Does it matter whether my NGO is registered in Delhi, Noida or Gurugram? For the state layer, yes — societies and trusts register with the state where they incorporate, so the registrar and local rules differ across Delhi, UP and Haryana. For everything funders verify — 12A, 80G, Darpan, CSR-1 and FCRA — the approvals are central and identical across NCR. We help you choose the incorporation state based on where your governing activity sits, then sequence the central registrations. Society, trust or Section 8 company — which structure should my NGO choose? A trust is simplest to form and run but concentrates control in trustees; a society suits member-driven organisations with elected governance but needs annual general-body compliance; a Section 8 company carries the highest credibility with corporate CSR donors and institutional funders, at the cost of full Companies Act compliance. All three can obtain 12A, 80G, Darpan, CSR-1 and FCRA. We recommend the structure based on who will fund you and who will govern you — then register it. What is CSR-1 registration, and can a brand-new NGO get it? CSR-1 is the mandatory MCA registration an NGO needs to legally receive corporate CSR funds — filed on the MCA portal with a DSC and certification by a practising CA/CS/CMA, generating a lifetime CSR registration number. Since mid-July 2025, newly-formed NGOs generally cannot file CSR-1 directly and must route projects through an already-eligible implementing agency; established NGOs with 12A/80G and a track record register directly. We advise the right route and file it. How do NGOs actually get CSR funding? Three things make you fundable: activities mapped to Schedule VII of the Companies Act (education, health, environment, livelihoods etc.), the compliance stack corporates verify (12A, 80G, Darpan, CSR-1), and targeted outreach — companies' CSR-2 filings publicly disclose what they fund and through whom, which is a prospecting map most NGOs never use. Listed-company CSR spend alone crossed Rs 22,000 crore in FY 2024-25, with health and education dominating. We build the stack and the pitch. © 2026 Udyog Growth. What PESO covers PESO (Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation) licensing applies across the Petroleum Act 1934/Petroleum Rules 2002 (fuel storage, petrol pumps), the Explosives Act 1884/Explosives Rules 2008, the Gas Cylinder Rules 2016, and the SMPV(U) Rules 2016 for pressure vessels — LPG, ammonia and CO2 tanks among them. Petroleum storage licence — the process Step Detail Registration On the National Single Window System (NSWS) Application On the PESO portal — Form XIV for dispensing installations (petrol pumps), Form XV/XVI for other storage District NOC Under Rule 144, from the District Magistrate — usually usable for 3 years from issue, and typically the longest step Plan/layout approval With prescribed safety distances Construction & inspection Site built to approved plan, then inspected Licence grant Issued on satisfactory inspection Fees: for Form XV/XVI storage, the published schedule is ₹5,000 for the first 50 kL plus ₹50 per additional kL, capped at ₹50,000 per calendar year per class; amendments/transfers cost ₹2,000. Small diesel (Class B) storage below the exempt limit needs no licence but must still meet safety conditions — we confirm the exact exemption quantity for your case before advising either way. Renewal: apply on or before expiry. Late renewal within one year carries a late fee of one-fourth of the licence fee per three months of delay; beyond one year past expiry, you must file a fresh application with a new District NOC — there's no shortcut back. Typical timeline: 30-90 days from a complete application to grant, with the District NOC usually the step that determines how long the whole process actually takes. Who needs this New retail fuel outlets, LPG distributors, industrial diesel or furnace-oil storage, CNG and SMPV pressure-vessel installations, and fireworks traders ahead of the festive season. Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions How much diesel can I store without a PESO licence? Up to 2,500 litres of Class B petroleum (diesel) in non-bulk storage without a licence. Above that, a DG-set or factory tank needs a licence — Form XIII from the District Authority for non-bulk storage up to 25,000 litres, or a PESO Circle licence for bulk installations. What is the fee for a small PESO petroleum licence? From the First Schedule: Form XII (Class A up to 300 L) ₹200 a year; Form XIII (Class B up to 25,000 L) ₹20 per 1,000 litres a year; Form XI (transport) ₹500 a year. Bulk-storage fees are per the current PESO user-charges schedule. Is a District Magistrate NOC required for a PESO licence? For retail outlets and bulk installations, yes — the DM/DC's NOC on site suitability precedes the PESO licence; in Delhi it is the revenue-district DM, in Noida the Gautam Buddh Nagar DM, in Gurugram and Faridabad the DC, in Patna the DM. Do I need a PESO licence for a diesel tank running my DG set? Only above the exempt storage quantities for that petroleum class — below the exempt limit no licence is needed, though safety rules still apply. We check your exact tank capacity against the current exemption limits before advising either way. What's the first step for a petrol pump or fuel-storage licence? Register on the National Single Window System, apply on the PESO portal using the relevant form (Form XIV for installations with dispensing, like petrol pumps), and obtain the District Magistrate's NOC under Rule 144 — this NOC is usually the longest step in the whole process. How long does PESO approval typically take? Commonly 30-90 days from a complete application, not counting the time needed for the District Magistrate's NOC or any construction work — the DM NOC specifically is the step most likely to add delay. What if my PESO licence has already expired? You can renew within one year of expiry by paying a late fee of one-fourth of the licence fee per three-month period of delay. Beyond one year past expiry, renewal isn't possible — you'll need a fresh application with a new District Magistrate NOC. Is the PESO application process online? Yes — fully online through PESO's own portal, integrated with the National Single Window System, including fee payment. PESO is the first department to have all of its licensing modules integrated with NSWS at transaction level. What does a PESO licence actually cost? For storage licences (Form XV/XVI), the published fee schedule is ₹5,000 for the first 50 kilolitres plus ₹50 per additional kilolitre, capped at ₹50,000 per calendar year per class; amendments or transfers cost ₹2,000. No. The 35% subsidy is credit-linked — it is released to your loan account with the bank after loan sanction, and gets credited as subsidy after three years of timely EMI payment with the unit operational and the loan account standard. What documents are needed for a PMFME application? PAN, Aadhaar, proof of enterprise, project report (DPR), land/rental documents, quotations for machinery, bank statements and Udyam registration. One District One Product — each district has an identified food product based on raw material availability and market strength. Generally, PMFME favours units not yet operational, or existing units expanding capacity — spending before sanction can affect eligibility for that specific expenditure. Is there a minimum or maximum project cost for PMFME? There's no fixed minimum, but the subsidy caps at Rs 10 lakh (35% of eligible cost), so very large projects will exceed the ceiling for the excess portion. Both, structured together — you take a bank loan for your project, and PMFME's 35% credit-linked subsidy (up to Rs 10 lakh) is adjusted into that same loan account after sanction. It's sometimes called the 'PMFME loan scheme' because the subsidy only flows through an actual bank loan; there's no separate cash grant without one. The sequence — and where each approval actually sits Land status first. If your site is agricultural land, Change of Land Use (CLU) or NA conversion from the state revenue authority comes before anything else — building on unconverted land creates problems no later approval can fix retroactively. Category assessment — the step that changes everything. Your project gets classified Red, Orange, Green or White by the Pollution Control Board based on Pollution Index. White category units don't need CTE or CTO at all — just a simple intimation to the Board. We've seen MSMEs spend weeks preparing a full CTE application when they legally only needed a one-page filing. Getting this classification right before you file anything is the single biggest time-and-fee saver in the whole process; filing under the wrong category is also the most common rejection reason we see. CTE (Consent to Establish). Applied for before construction, based on your proposed design — pollution control systems, waste handling, and site NOC from the local authority. Valid for 5 years, extendable up to 7 — and any material change to your process, machinery or capacity after approval needs a fresh CTE, not an amendment. Environmental Clearance, where applicable. For EIA-listed projects, run in parallel with or before CTE — includes public hearing records and third-party assessment for Red-category units. CTO (Consent to Operate). Applied for once construction is complete, with lab-tested proof — effluent quality, stack emissions, ambient air readings, documented ETP/STP specifications, and a Chartered Accountant's capital investment certificate. This is what lets you legally start commercial operations. Renewal cycle. Both CTE and CTO carry validity periods and need renewal before expiry — we track this so a lapsed consent doesn't become an operational shutdown. Location Pollution authority Delhi DPCC Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad UPPCB Gurugram, Faridabad HSPCB Determined by where the unit physically sits, not where your head office is. And in Delhi, White-category activities don't need CTE/CTO at all — only an online undertaking to DPCC — while Red, Orange and Green categories must apply through the online portal. Getting the category and the board right first saves weeks. Two approvals that sit adjacent to consents in most projects: if your site is agricultural land, land conversion / CLU comes before CTE in the sequence — and if the project includes rooftop solar, our solar subsidy & net-metering practice handles the DISCOM side. DPCC consent validity — Red 5 years, Orange 10, Green 15 (official policy): Consent to Establish is granted for 1–7 years. White-category units need no CTE/CTO and file an online undertaking instead. Applications are online only — there is no offline route. Dedicated coordination — consistent follow-up on your application so it keeps moving through the standard workflow. Compliance-first documentation — built to withstand scrutiny, protecting your business from future audits or objections. Frequently Asked Questions What's the difference between CTE and CTO? CTE (Consent to Establish) is the approval you need before you build or set up a plant — it confirms your proposed pollution-control design is acceptable. CTO (Consent to Operate) comes after construction, confirming what you actually built and installed matches what was consented, and that it's performing within limits. You need CTE first, then CTO before you start commercial operations — running without either invites closure orders, not just fines. Does every business need Environmental Clearance (EC), or just CTE/CTO? Not every business needs EC — it's specifically required for projects listed in the EIA Notification 2006, based on sector and investment size (thermal power, mining, large industrial units, certain infrastructure projects, and more). Smaller units in Green or White category (per Pollution Control Board classification) often need CTE/CTO only, not EC. We assess which category your project falls into before you spend on the wrong process. What documents does a Pollution Control Board actually check for CTO? Accredited lab test reports for treated effluent quality, stack emission levels and ambient air quality (usually within the last 3-6 months), and details of your installed pollution-control equipment — ETP, STP, stack emission controls, noise attenuation — with make, model and treatment capacity. For Red-category projects, public hearing records and third-party environmental assessments may also be required. Which authority handles land conversion for setting up a unit? Change of Land Use (CLU) or Non-Agricultural (NA) conversion is handled by the state revenue/development authority, not the Pollution Control Board — it's a separate, earlier step if your land is currently agricultural. We sequence this before CTE where relevant, since starting construction on unconverted land creates a compounding problem later. Is there a subsidy for solar power under MNRE? Yes — MNRE and state nodal agencies run capital subsidy and net-metering support for rooftop and captive solar, plus PPA (Power Purchase Agreement) facilitation for larger installations. We handle the subsidy application alongside any land/environmental clearances the installation itself needs. Does every small business need CTE and CTO? No — White category units (the lowest pollution-index classification, covering many service and low-impact businesses) are exempt from CTE and CTO entirely; they only need to file a simple intimation with the Pollution Control Board. Getting your category verified before assuming you need a full CTE application can save weeks of unnecessary paperwork. How long is a CTE valid, and can I change my project after getting one? CTE is initially valid for 5 years, extendable up to a maximum of 7 if the project isn't completed in time. But any material change afterward — different machinery, a revised production capacity, changed raw materials, or an altered layout — requires a fresh CTE, not an amendment; operating outside what was originally consented risks CTO rejection later. My factory is in Noida but my office is in Delhi — which pollution board do I apply to? Consent follows the polluting activity, not the head office: a Noida or Ghaziabad unit files with UPPCB, a Gurugram or Faridabad unit with HSPCB, and a Delhi unit with DPCC. A Delhi office that falls in the White category may need only an online undertaking rather than full CTE/CTO. We determine your category and jurisdiction first, then file with the right board. Do I need Environmental Clearance, or just CTE/CTO consent? They're different layers. CTE/CTO consents from the state board (DPCC, UPPCB or HSPCB in NCR) apply to every Red, Orange or Green category unit — most factories need only these. Environmental Clearance under the EIA notification is a separate, project-level approval required only for listed activity categories and scales, typically large industrial, mining, construction or infrastructure projects. We first determine whether your project triggers EC at all, then sequence EC (if needed) before CTE, before construction. © 2026 Udyog Growth. A regulatory affairs consultant prepares and files your applications to departmental standards, tracks the file through the government system, responds to queries and show-cause notices on your behalf, represents you at hearings and inspections, and coordinates between departments where an approval touches more than one authority. The work is procedural and representational — we do not have the power to approve anything ourselves. What is the difference between regulatory affairs support and a government approval itself? Regulatory affairs support is the professional service of preparing your file correctly and representing you before the department; the approval itself is issued only by the government authority, on merit, through its own process. The Rs 5 lakh "security deposit" myth: widely repeated online, but there is no such mandatory deposit for a senior secondary school. The Rs 5,00,000 figure in CBSE's fee schedule is the society-to-society transfer fee — a completely different head. Official fresh-affiliation fees are far lower: Rs 1,50,000 up to Secondary, Rs 2,50,000 up to Senior Secondary, plus Rs 5,000 annual. We work from the current fee schedule, not recycled blog numbers. CBSE affiliation — eligibility, land, fees Only a registered Society, Public Trust or Section 8 company can hold CBSE affiliation — never a proprietary or for-profit company. Affiliation is staged: fresh affiliation up to Secondary first (initial term 3 years), Senior Secondary comes by upgradation after running Classes 9-10, then 5-year extension cycles. Land category Where Minimum land Category C Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad + NE/island states 1,600–2,400 sq m Category B Y-category cities, state capitals, hilly areas 2,400–3,200 sq m Category A Anywhere else 6,000 sq m Land only sets your category now — sections are decided by built-up area (3 sections per 400 sq m, certified by the local body or a licensed architect). This decoupling, clarified via CBSE Notification No. 06/2026, changes how much you can actually run on a given plot — a distinction most consultants still get wrong. Fee head Amount Fresh affiliation up to Senior Secondary ₹2,50,000 Fresh affiliation up to Secondary ₹1,50,000 Middle Class Syllabus (Classes 1–5) ₹50,000 Annual fee ₹5,000 Re-inspection / periodical inspection ₹50,000 each Society-to-society transfer ₹5,00,000 SARAS 7.0 — the current application cycle CBSE now runs affiliation through the SARAS portal (currently version 7.0) . Two pre-conditions before you can even file: a UDISE+ code and a completed SQAAF self-assessment . Fresh affiliation and upgradation applications now attract a mandatory 100% physical inspection — there is no longer a documents-only fast track. We track every SARAS window and portal update so a client's file is ready the day it opens, not scrambling after a deadline extension. CISCE / ICSE affiliation The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations affiliates schools to a similarly non-profit entity (Society/Trust/Section 8 company), with comparable land, staffing and PTR expectations, a qualified principal (5+ years' experience), and a properly constituted managing committee. CISCE affiliation hinges heavily on the inspection report — we prepare the file and the premises together, not sequentially. Delhi Directorate of Education recognition The DoE has scrapped the old "essentiality certificate" requirement and moved to a self-certification model — a school certifies against a checklist of infrastructure, safety, teacher and PTR standards (73 checkpoints, down from 91) rather than waiting on a discretionary essentiality clearance. Recognition under the Delhi School Education Act & Rules, 1973 remains mandatory regardless of CBSE's own optional-NOC change — the two are separate documents, and a school still needs the State Recognition Certificate before its CBSE/CISCE file can go through. Since November 2025 , the DoE has also moved to recognise private unaided schools operating in previously non-conforming areas — bringing an estimated ~500 additional schools under DoE oversight and creating roughly 20,000 extra EWS/DG/CWSN seats citywide. If your school (or a site you're evaluating) sits in an area that was earlier treated as non-conforming, this is worth re-checking before assuming recognition is blocked. RTE compliance & the 25% EWS quota Private unaided non-minority schools must reserve 25% of entry-level seats for EWS/DG students under Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act, with state fee reimbursement under Section 12(2). Delhi runs a computerised EWS lottery (the 2025-26 draw allotted around 42,000 seats). A Supreme Court bench, by order dated 13 January 2026, directed that securing this quota be treated as a national mission and impleaded the NCPCR to monitor compliance — enforcement is tightening, not easing. We help schools build the compliant admission and reimbursement-claim process from the outset rather than fixing it under audit pressure. UDISE+ registration The 11-digit UDISE+ code is filed via Form A02 through your Block/District MIS office — not a self-serve online form — and requires state recognition first. Realistic timelines run 4-6 weeks in metros to 8-12 weeks in rural areas; the July-September window gets congested. Since UDISE+ is itself a SARAS pre-condition, a delay here delays affiliation. Fire & building safety NOC for schools An educational building in Delhi taller than 9 m or with ground plus 2 upper storeys needs a fire safety certificate under the Delhi Fire Service Act 2007 and NBC 2016 Part 4 — a two-stage process (pre-construction plan approval, then post-construction certification), typically valid 3 years, filed through the Delhi Fire Service. A separate building-safety/structural-stability certificate from the local body or a licensed architect is required for CBSE regardless of the fire NOC. School canteen FSSAI, entity formation & educational land Three approvals in this journey are already deep specialities of ours on other pages — we run them as one file for a school client rather than three separate engagements: FSSAI registration/license for the canteen or hostel mess (HFSS-food restrictions apply within and near school premises), Society/Trust/Section 8 company formation for the school's managing body, and change of land use (CLU) for educational purposes in Delhi if the site isn't already zoned for institutional use. School bus & transport compliance CBSE-mandated norms (implementing Supreme Court guidelines under the Motor Vehicles Act 1988): yellow paint with "School Bus"/"On School Duty" signage, a speed governor capped at 40 km/h, GPS and CCTV, grilled windows with mesh, a female attendant, a trained driver with a clean record, a designated Transport Manager, and a valid RTO permit from the state transport department. Delhi school fee law — status, verified 4 October 2026: the Delhi School Education (Transparency in Fixation and Regulation of Fees) Act, 2025 was notified on 14 August 2025 and its Rules on 10 December 2025. It applies to all ~1,700 private unaided schools (the 1973 Act regime covered about 300), permits only defined fee heads, requires a School-Level Fee Regulation Committee (5 parents by draw, 3 teachers, 1 government observer) to approve revisions, and mandates refund with interest of unauthorised fees. The Supreme Court recorded on 2 February 2026 that it would not apply to 2025-26; the government committed to 2026-27. On 28 February 2026 the Delhi High Court deferred the direction to constitute SLFRCs for 2026-27 pending final hearing on the Act's validity — that challenge is still before the High Court , so check the latest order before relying on the Act for a fee dispute or a school's fee notice. Frequently Asked Questions What is the CBSE affiliation fee for a new school? ₹1,50,000 for fresh affiliation up to Secondary and ₹2,50,000 up to Senior Secondary (Bye-Laws 2018, Appendix-I), plus the ₹10,000 SARAS KYC registration; upgradation later costs ₹1,00,000. Late filing adds ₹25,000 a month up to ₹1,00,000. Is the Delhi school fee regulation Act in force for 2026-27? The Act (14 Aug 2025) and Rules (10 Dec 2025) are notified and the government committed to apply them from 2026-27, but the Delhi High Court deferred the School-Level Fee Regulation Committee direction on 28 February 2026 and is hearing the validity challenge. Status is therefore 'notified, implementation contested' — check the latest High Court order before acting on it. Is CBSE State NOC still mandatory for a new school in 2026? No — from the 2026-27 session, CBSE's State NOC is optional. A school can apply with or without it; if without, CBSE refers the matter to the state, and a deemed-NOC applies if the state stays silent for 30 days plus a 15-day reminder. This does not remove the separate, still-mandatory State Recognition Certificate under the RTE Act — the two are different documents. How much land do I need to open a CBSE school? It depends on land category: 1,600-2,400 sq m in Category C cities (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and a few other areas), 2,400-3,200 sq m in Category B, and 6,000 sq m in Category A elsewhere. Note land area now only sets your category — the number of sections you can actually run is governed separately by built-up area, at 3 sections per 400 sq m. How much does CBSE affiliation actually cost? Official fees: Rs 1,50,000 for fresh affiliation up to Secondary, Rs 2,50,000 up to Senior Secondary, Rs 50,000 for the Middle Class Syllabus (Classes 1-5), and Rs 5,000 annual. There is no mandatory Rs 5 lakh 'security deposit' for a senior secondary school — that figure is the separate society-to-society transfer fee, often misquoted online. Can a private company set up and run a CBSE school? No — CBSE only affiliates schools run by a registered Society, Public Trust or Section 8 (not-for-profit) company. A proprietary or for-profit private limited company cannot hold CBSE affiliation, so the first step for a new school is choosing and registering the right non-profit entity. What is SARAS 7.0 and what do I need before applying? SARAS is CBSE's online affiliation portal, currently on version 7.0. Two pre-conditions before filing: a UDISE+ code and a completed SQAAF self-assessment. Fresh affiliation and upgradation applications now require a mandatory 100% physical inspection — there's no documents-only route anymore. Do I need a UDISE+ code before applying for CBSE affiliation? Yes — UDISE+ is a precondition for filing on SARAS. It's an 11-digit code obtained via Form A02 through your Block/District MIS office (not a self-serve online form), and it requires state recognition to already be in place. Budget 4-6 weeks in metros to 8-12 weeks in rural areas, and avoid applying in the congested July-September window. What fire safety rules apply to a school building in Delhi? A school building taller than 9 m, or with ground plus 2 upper storeys, needs a Delhi Fire Service certificate under the Delhi Fire Service Act 2007 and NBC 2016 — a two-stage process covering pre-construction plan approval and post-construction certification, typically valid 3 years. This is separate from, and in addition to, the building-safety/structural-stability certificate CBSE requires. Is the 25% EWS quota compulsory for private schools, and is enforcement getting stricter? Yes — Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act requires private unaided non-minority schools to reserve 25% of entry-level seats for EWS/DG students, with state fee reimbursement. A Supreme Court bench, by order dated 13 January 2026, directed that this be treated as a national mission and brought in the NCPCR to monitor compliance — schools should expect tighter enforcement, not a rollback. My school's land was earlier in a "non-conforming area" — can it still be recognised? Possibly, and more easily than before. Since November 2025 the DoE has moved to recognise private unaided schools even in previously non-conforming areas, bringing an estimated 500 additional schools under its oversight. Zoning and land-use still need to be checked and, if required, regularised — but the blanket bar that existed earlier has been relaxed. Do I need a separate FSSAI license for the school canteen? Yes — canteens and hostel mess facilities need FSSAI Basic Registration or a State License depending on turnover, and FSSAI's charter separately restricts high-fat/sugar/salt (HFSS) food within and near school premises. We run this alongside the affiliation file rather than as an afterthought — see our dedicated FSSAI page for the full slab and process detail. What happens if my CBSE affiliation extension lapses? A lapsed extension puts the school's ability to conduct board exams and issue valid certificates at risk. Extension fees are tiered by how late you apply (Rs 50,000-1,50,000) plus a late fee of Rs 25,000/month capped at Rs 1,00,000 — so the cost of delay compounds quickly. We track extension timelines for clients well before the 5-year cycle turns over. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Paid by DBT, typically 30–45 days after DISCOM commissioning. Apply on pmsuryaghar.gov.in; equipment must be ALMM-listed ; group housing societies get ₹18,000/kW for common facilities up to 500 kW. Last verified 4 October 2026 — rules on this page checked against the current notifications. We update it the day a rule changes. The #1 reason subsidy claims get rejected: a panel or inverter that isn't on the MNRE ALMM list — followed by the electricity-connection name not matching the applicant. Both are checked after you've spent the money, so we verify vendor, equipment and paperwork before installation, not at claim stage. What you actually get System size Subsidy 1 kW ₹30,000 2 kW ₹60,000 3 kW and above ₹78,000 (cap) Group housing society / RWA (common facilities) ₹18,000 per kW, up to 500 kW (max 3 kW per house) Eligibility: a residential electricity connection with sanctioned load up to 10 kW, the application in the same name as the electricity bill, and no earlier rooftop-solar subsidy on the connection. We check your eligibility and vendor's equipment against this list before installation starts — catching a disqualifying issue after the panels are up is far more expensive than catching it before. State top-ups on the central subsidy — Delhi, UP, Bihar, Haryana State Additional state subsidy (residential) 3 kW total with ₹78,000 central How it is claimed Delhi ₹10,000 per kW, capped at ₹30,000 — plus a generation-based incentive of ₹3 per unit for 5 years (Delhi Solar Policy 2024) ₹1,08,000 + GBI Separate application on the Delhi solar portal after the central claim; DISCOM (BSES / Tata Power-DDL) net meter Uttar Pradesh (Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad) ₹15,000 per kW, capped at ₹30,000 (UPNEDA) ₹1,08,000 Through the UPNEDA / state section of the national portal; UPPCL (PVVNL) net meter Bihar (Patna) ₹10,000 per kW, capped at ₹20,000 per consumer — approved by the Bihar Cabinet on 12 August 2026 (₹1,000 crore outlay) ₹98,000 BREDA / state module; NBPDCL–SBPDCL net meter Haryana (Gurugram, Faridabad) No general residential top-up notified as of 4 October 2026 (category-specific support only) ₹78,000 DHBVN net meter Central slabs: ₹30,000 for the first kW, ₹30,000 for the second, ₹18,000 for the third — ₹78,000 cap at 3 kW and above. The state amount is a second application with its own vendor and inspection conditions; most "subsidy missing" complaints we see are a central claim paid and a state claim never filed. The claim sequence — where files get stuck Portal registration on pmsuryaghar.gov.in with DISCOM and consumer number. Feasibility approval from the DISCOM — sanctioned-load and technical checks happen here. Installation by a registered vendor with ALMM-listed panels and inverter — the step where a wrong equipment choice silently kills the subsidy. Net metering + commissioning — meter installation and DISCOM inspection. DBT disbursal — bank details on the portal; money typically lands 30–45 days after commissioning. We chase every stage so the file never idles. Commercial & industrial rooftops — a different game PM Surya Ghar is residential; shops, offices and factories don't get this subsidy. Commercial rooftop works on economics instead: net-metering/net-billing arrangements with your DISCOM, capex-vs-PPA structuring (third-party investor owns the plant, you buy power cheaper), and the accounting treatment of the asset. We structure the DISCOM approvals and the PPA so the project stands on savings, not on a subsidy that doesn't exist for you. Factory or commercial installation as part of a bigger setup? Solar sits alongside pollution consents and the project-finance file — we handle the full approval stack.
